issue_snapshot.title: task-run-recorder bulk upserts fragment to one row per INSERT statement
issue_snapshot.body:
### Bug summary

The recorder batches task run rows for bulk insert, but almost every batch ends up holding one row. A flush of 300 task runs runs 300 separate INSERT statements.

So the service spends its time waiting on database round trips rather than doing work, and falls behind under load. You can't scale it out either, because concurrent replicas deadlock (#21587).

It also has a knock-on effect outside the service. Redis stream trimming uses the lowest `last-delivered-id` across all consumer groups ([`prefect_redis/messaging.py:784-821`](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/7d377adfd43019a26cc901d7f50491489a86377f/src/integrations/prefect-redis/prefect_redis/messaging.py#L784-L821)), so a recorder that lags stops the stream getting trimmed for everyone else.

This only shows up if you raise `PREFECT_SERVER_SERVICES_TASK_RUN_RECORDER_BATCH_SIZE`. It defaults to 1, and at that setting a flush holds one event, so there is nothing to batch.

#### Reproduction

No server or Redis needed. Save as `repro.py` and run `uv run -s repro.py`. Pass a database URL as the first argument to try PostgreSQL.

```python
"""task-run-recorder fragments its bulk upserts into one row per INSERT."""

import asyncio
import sys
import tempfile
from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy import event

from prefect.server.database import provide_database_interface
from prefect.server.events.schemas.events import ReceivedEvent
from prefect.server.services.task_run_recorder import record_bulk_task_run_events
from prefect.settings import PREFECT_API_DATABASE_CONNECTION_URL, temporary_settings

WHEN = "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"

# The client emitter dumps the task run with exclude_none=True, so which optional
# fields are present varies from one event to the next.
VARIANTS = [
    {},
    {"start_time": WHEN},
    {"task_version": "1.0"},
    {"cache_key": "abc123"},
    {"start_time": WHEN, "task_version": "1.0"},
]


def task_run_event(i: int) -> ReceivedEvent:
    return ReceivedEvent(
        id=UUID(int=i),
        occurred=WHEN,
        event="prefect.task-run.Running",
        # sequential ids so the recorder's sort order is deterministic
        resource={"prefect.resource.id": f"prefect.task-run.{UUID(int=i)}"},
        payload={
            "validated_state": {"type": "RUNNING"},
            "task_run": {
                "task_key": "my_task-abc123",
                "dynamic_key": str(i),
                **VARIANTS[i % len(VARIANTS)],
            },
        },
    )


async def main() -> None:
    db = provide_database_interface()
    await db.create_db()

    inserts: list[str] = []

    def count_inserts(conn, cursor, statement, parameters, context, executemany):
        if statement.lstrip().startswith("INSERT INTO task_run ("):
            inserts.append(statement)

    event.listen(
        (await db.engine()).sync_engine, "before_cursor_execute", count_inserts
    )

    await record_bulk_task_run_events([task_run_event(i) for i in range(300)])
    print(f"300 task runs -> {len(inserts)} INSERT statements")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # optional argv[1]: a database URL, such as a PostgreSQL DSN
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        url = (
            sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else f"sqlite+aiosqlite:///{tmp}/repro.db"
        )
        with temporary_settings({PREFECT_API_DATABASE_CONNECTION_URL: url}):
            asyncio.run(main())
```

Same output on SQLite and PostgreSQL:

```text
300 task runs -> 300 INSERT statements
```

#### Why it happens

`_record_bulk_task_run_events` batches rows by `(frozenset(task_run_dict.keys()), conflict_target)` and merges only neighbours whose key matches exactly ([`task_run_recorder.py:336-348`](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/7d377adfd43019a26cc901d7f50491489a86377f/src/prefect/server/services/task_run_recorder.py#L336-L348)). The rows arrive sorted by `_task_run_upsert_key` ([`:261-264`](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/7d377adfd43019a26cc901d7f50491489a86377f/src/prefect/server/services/task_run_recorder.py#L261-L264)), and that sort has nothing to do with either half of the batch key:

- The column set changes from one event to the next. The client emitter dumps with `exclude_none=True` ([`utilities/engine/__init__.py:932-934`](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/7d377adfd43019a26cc901d7f50491489a86377f/src/prefect/utilities/engine/__init__.py#L932-L934)), the server's `exclude_unset=True` keeps that variance, and so `start_time`, `end_time`, `cache_key` and `task_version` come and go.
- `conflict_target` is worked out per row from what is already in the database ([`:310-334`](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/7d377adfd43019a26cc901d7f50491489a86377f/src/prefect/server/services/task_run_recorder.py#L310-L334)), so it flips part way through a flush.

Matching keys are therefore rarely neighbours. In the script above no two adjacent rows match, which is why every row gets its own statement.

#### A possible fix

Today a batch ends as soon as the next row's batch key differs. It should end only when the next row genuinely cannot share a statement with the rows already in it.

Two rows can share a statement when they upsert on the same conflict target and their column sets can be merged.

Merging means widening the statement to every column either row has, and passing `NULL` for the ones a row does not supply. The `SET` clause then uses `coalesce(excluded.col, task_run.col)`, so a `NULL` filler leaves the stored value alone instead of wiping it.

That covers most columns but not all, so a batch still has to close before a row that:

- upserts on a different conflict target
- would need a `NULL` in a column where `NULL` is not the same as absent: one with a default, one in the `ON CONFLICT` target, or the one the `WHERE` clause filters on
- repeats a conflict target value already in the batch, which PostgreSQL rejects
- pushes the batch past the driver's bind parameter limit

All of this is one pass, left to right, so batches stay contiguous runs of the sorted list, which is what keeps the #22112 guarantee intact. Grouping by key across the whole flush would collapse more statements, but #22112 ruled that out: a sorted input like `A, B, A` could then run as `A, A, B`, which breaks the lock ordering #21717 added to stop concurrent recorders deadlocking.

On the script above this gives 1 statement on PostgreSQL and 8 on SQLite. SQLite is lower because Prefect caps bind parameters at 999.

### Version info

```Text
Version:              3.8.2
API version:          0.8.4
Python version:       3.11.15
Git commit:           7d377adf
OS/Arch:              linux/x86_64
Server type:          server
Pydantic version:     2.13.4
Server:
  Database:           sqlite
```

Also reproduced against postgres:14.

### Additional context

#### Related

- #21587 (open): concurrent replicas deadlock, so scaling out is not a workaround.
- #21716 (closed): horizontal scaling for this service.
- #21456 (closed): a separate throughput bottleneck in the same service.
- #22112, #21726, #21717, #19586: the changes that produced the current batching.

#### A second, unrelated bug in the same function

`conflict_target`'s canonical-id fallback rewrites `task_run.id`. That changes the row's upsert key part way through the flush, so a lookup further down misses and raises `KeyError`. It is not an `IntegrityError`, so nothing retries it: `flush()` puts the batch back on the queue and eventually drops every event in it. Reproduces on unmodified `main`, and has nothing to do with batching.

issue_snapshot.title: Self-hosted `PrefectEventsClient` never authenticates its `/events/in` WebSocket connection — task run events silently dropped when `PREFECT_SERVER_API_AUTH_STRING` is set
issue_snapshot.body:
## Bug summary

When basic auth (`PREFECT_SERVER_API_AUTH_STRING` / `PREFECT_API_AUTH_STRING`) is enabled on a self-hosted server, the client's outbound events-publishing WebSocket connection (`wss://<host>/api/events/in`) always fails with `HTTP 401`, regardless of whether valid credentials are configured. This isn't cosmetic — task run state changes are published via this channel, so **`task_runs` never persist server-side** while flow runs continue to work normally. The failure is silent unless you notice the `WARNING | prefect.events.clients - Unable to connect to 'wss://.../api/events/in' ... HTTP 401` log line.

## Reproduction

1. Self-hosted server with `PREFECT_SERVER_API_AUTH_STRING=admin:pass` set (reproduced via the official `prefect-server` Helm chart, and via `prefect server start` directly).
2. Client with matching `PREFECT_API_AUTH_STRING=admin:pass`.
3. Run any flow with at least one task.

**Expected:** Task run states persist server-side, visible in `/api/task_runs/filter`.

**Actual:**
```
WARNING | prefect.events.clients - Unable to connect to 'wss://<host>/api/events/in'. ... server rejected WebSocket connection: HTTP 401.
ERROR   | GlobalEventLoopThread | prefect._internal.concurrency - Service 'EventsWorker' failed with N pending items.
```
And subsequently:
```
curl -u "admin:pass" -X POST https://<host>/api/task_runs/count -d '{}'
0
```
even after multiple successful flow runs — `flow_runs` persist fine (REST-orchestrated, unaffected), but `task_runs` never do.

## Root cause

Confirmed via a raw handshake test against the server directly, bypassing the Python client entirely:

```
# No Authorization header:
$ curl -i -N -H "Connection: Upgrade" -H "Upgrade: websocket" ... https://<host>/api/events/in
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"exception_message":"Unauthorized"}

# With Authorization: Basic <base64(admin:pass)> header:
$ curl -i -N -u "admin:pass" -H "Connection: Upgrade" -H "Upgrade: websocket" ... https://<host>/api/events/in
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
{"detail":"Not Found"}
```

The second response seems to be key: adding the header gets the request **past** the server's basic-auth middleware and into normal routing (it only 404s because plain `curl` doesn't perform a real WebSocket handshake — this is not an auth failure). This confirms the server accepts Basic Auth on the `/events/in` handshake correctly, and that nothing in the network path (reverse proxy, ingress, etc.) is the problem.

However, the client never sends this header on this specific connection. In `src/prefect/events/clients.py`, `PrefectEventsClient.__init__` (the self-hosted events-emitting client) captures the auth string:

```python
auth_string = get_current_settings().api.auth_string
self._auth_token = (
    auth_string.get_secret_value() if auth_string is not None else None
)
self._events_socket_url = events_in_socket_from_api_url(api_url)
self._connect = websocket_connect(
    self._events_socket_url,
    subprotocols=[Subprotocol("prefect")],
)
```

`self._auth_token` is captured but never attached to `websocket_connect()` — no `additional_headers` are passed. It's only sent later as a post-connect JSON message (`{"type": "auth", "token": self._auth_token}`), which never gets a chance to be read because the server's Basic Auth middleware already rejects the handshake's initial HTTP request first.

Compare to `PrefectCloudEventsClient`, a few lines down in the same file, which does attach credentials at the HTTP layer:

```python
self._connect = websocket_connect(
    self._events_socket_url,
    additional_headers={"Authorization": f"bearer {api_key}"},
)
```

## Related issues

- #17687 originally reported that the events WebSocket didn't enforce auth *at all* — a security hole.
- #17741 fixed that, but only for `PrefectEventSubscriber` (the *read* side — `/events/out`, used by `prefect events stream`). It didn't touch `PrefectEventsClient` (the *emit* side — `/events/in`), which is what flow/task runs actually use to publish state changes. This issue is that remaining gap.
- #20474 / #20537 are superficially similar (`401`/`403` on the events WebSocket) but were caused by a client/server version mismatch during the 3.6.14→3.6.15 window and were resolved by pinning versions. This issue reproduces on **matching, current versions** (client and server both `3.8.2`), so it's a distinct, still-open gap.

## Version info

```
Version:              3.8.2
API version:          0.8.4
Python version:       3.12.13
Server type:          self-hosted (Helm chart), basic auth enabled
```
Also reproduced against client `3.4.20` against the same server — not a regression tied to a specific client version.

## Suggested fix

Mirror the `PrefectCloudEventsClient` pattern in `PrefectEventsClient.__init__` — attach `additional_headers={"Authorization": f"Basic {base64.b64encode(self._auth_token.encode()).decode()}"}` to the `websocket_connect()` call when `self._auth_token` is set. Happy to open a PR for this if a maintainer can confirm this is the right approach — flagging first per the contribution guide rather than jumping straight to a PR.

issue_snapshot.title: Crash `AttributeError: 'For' object has no attribute 'value'` when `x.__class__` is a for-loop, `with`, or unpacking target
issue_snapshot.body:
### Bug description

During a code correctness review of the class checker I found that any code where `x.__class__` appears as an assignment target *outside* a plain assignment statement makes the whole module fail with a fatal `astroid-error` (F0002), so every other message for that file is lost.

Minimal reproducer:

```python
class Foo:
    pass


def f(foo):
    for foo.__class__ in [Foo]:
        pass
```

`_check_invalid_class_object` assumes the parent of the `AssignAttr` is a plain assignment with a `.value`, but for a `for` loop target the parent is the `For` node:

```
Exception on node <AssignAttr.__class__ l.6 at 0x...> in file 'crash_for.py'
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "pylint/utils/ast_walker.py", line 87, in walk
    callback(astroid)
  File "pylint/checkers/classes/class_checker.py", line 1735, in visit_assignattr
    self._check_invalid_class_object(node)
  File "pylint/checkers/classes/class_checker.py", line 1751, in _check_invalid_class_object
    inferred = safe_infer(node.parent.value)
AttributeError: 'For' object has no attribute 'value'
crash_for.py:1:0: F0002: crash_for.py: Fatal error while checking 'crash_for.py'. ... (astroid-error)
```

The same unchecked assumptions crash on the whole family of legal (if unusual) constructs — all reproduced locally on `main` (4be9585) and 4.0.7:

```python
with ctx as foo.__class__: ...            # AttributeError: 'With' object has no attribute 'value'
[0 for foo.__class__ in [Foo]]            # AttributeError: 'Comprehension' object has no attribute 'value'
foo.__class__: type                       # AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'infer'
foo.__class__, x = get_pair()             # AttributeError: 'Call' object has no attribute 'elts'   (line 1749)
for foo.__class__, x in [(Foo, 1)]: ...   # AttributeError: 'For' object has no attribute 'value'   (line 1749)
(a.x, foo.__class__), y = (1, Foo), 2     # AttributeError: 'ClassDef' object has no attribute 'value'
x, foo.__class__ = (Foo,)                 # IndexError: list index out of range
```

The `assigning-non-slot` path has the same problem when the instance's class defines `__slots__`, in `_check_in_slots` (line 1827, `node.parent.value` again) and in `_has_same_layout_slots` (line 483, `next(assigned_value.infer())` without handling `astroid.InferenceError`):

```python
class A:
    __slots__ = ["x"]

class B:
    __slots__ = ["x"]

def f():
    inst = A()
    for inst.__class__ in [B]:       # AttributeError: 'For' object has no attribute 'value' (line 1827)
        pass
    inst.__class__, y = B, 1         # AttributeError: 'ClassDef' object has no attribute 'value' (line 1827)
    inst.__class__ = UndefinedName   # astroid.exceptions.NameInferenceError (line 483)
```

This is the remaining family of #7467: the fix for that issue added the tuple-unpacking branch, but only for a literal right-hand side in a plain `Assign`, and the slots code path was not covered.

### Configuration

```ini
# none needed; reproduces with an empty configuration
```

### Command used

```shell
pylint --disable=all --enable=invalid-class-object,assigning-non-slot crash_for.py
```

### Pylint output

```shell
crash_for.py:1:0: F0002: crash_for.py: Fatal error while checking 'crash_for.py'. Please open an issue in our bug tracker so we address this. ... (astroid-error)
```

(full tracebacks above)

### Expected behavior

No crash. issue_snapshot.title: ListField does not respect ordered sequence in form data with partial updates.
issue_snapshot.body:
## Checklist

- [X] I have verified that that issue exists against the `master` branch of Django REST framework.
- [X] I have searched for similar issues in both open and closed tickets and cannot find a duplicate.
- [X] This is not a usage question. (Those should be directed to the [discussion group](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/django-rest-framework) instead.)
- [X] This cannot be dealt with as a third party library. (We prefer new functionality to be [in the form of third-party libraries](http://www.django-rest-framework.org/topics/third-party-resources/#about-third-party-packages) where possible.)
- [X] I have reduced the issue to the simplest possible case.
- [ ] I have included a failing test as a pull request. (If you are unable to do so we can still accept the issue.)

## Steps to reproduce

1. For example, we have serializer like this:

```python
class CommunitySerializer(Serializer):

    colors = ListField(allow_null=True, child=CharField(label='Colors', max_length=7), required=False)
```

2. We submit partial update encoded as form data:

```python
test_client.patch('/communities/1/', {'colors[0]': '#ffffff', 'colors[1]': '#000000'}, 'multipart')
```

3. This will encode request body like this:

```
--BoUnDaRyStRiNg
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="colors[0]"

#000000
--BoUnDaRyStRiNg
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="colors[1]"

#ffffff
--BoUnDaRyStRiNg--
```

## Expected behavior

`validated_data` should contain colors value parsed into a list with the respected order.

## Actual behavior

`validated_data` is an empty dictionary.

## Explanation

1. `ListField.get_value` checks that field is present with `in` statement:

https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/blob/ed6340ee7619d7e8c3419ffacb973f7ca0c329d3/rest_framework/fields.py#L1639

2. Since `field_name` does not match submitted keys, method checks in this is a partial update

https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/blob/ed6340ee7619d7e8c3419ffacb973f7ca0c329d3/rest_framework/fields.py#L1640

3. Since this is also true, the method returns an empty marker.

https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/blob/ed6340ee7619d7e8c3419ffacb973f7ca0c329d3/rest_framework/fields.py#L1641

4. Field name with ordered marker does not check to present.

## Alternative

We can submit the partial update with list fields unordered:

```python
test_client.patch('/communities/1/', {'colors': ['#ffffff', '#000000']}, 'multipart')
```

Form data will look like this

```
--BoUnDaRyStRiNg
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="colors"

#000000
--BoUnDaRyStRiNg
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="colors"

#ffffff
--BoUnDaRyStRiNg--
```

So `in` statement will evaluate to true, so dictionary will be processed by HTML parser.

https://github.com/encode/django-rest-framework/blob/ed6340ee7619d7e8c3419ffacb973f7ca0c329d3/rest_framework/fields.py#L1649

But this format does not guarantee items order in the list, so we can not use it for things like gradients.

Full update and create methods do not have this problem because partial check evaluates to false.

We can't use full updates because we have two file fields near. We don't want to force the user to upload two files just to change string values in the same request.

## P.S.

If you think we should solve this, I'll be able to make a PR for it.

issue_snapshot.title: False positive `possibly-used-before-assignment` for `-> typing.NoReturn`
issue_snapshot.body:
`-> NoReturn` is treated as terminating (#9674 / #9714), but the qualified form
`-> typing.NoReturn` is not. `typing.Never` behaves the same.

```python
import typing

def terminate(msg) -> typing.NoReturn:
    raise SystemExit(msg)

def f(flag):
    if flag:
        cmd = "ls"
    else:
        terminate("nope")
    return cmd  # E0606
```

`utils.is_terminating_func` requires `isinstance(inferred.returns, nodes.Name)`, so the
`nodes.Attribute` annotation never reaches the qname check that already knows
`typing.NoReturn`. `RefactoringChecker._is_function_def_never_returning` accepts both,
so `inconsistent-return-statements` is unaffected.

No message, and `unreachable` after such a call (same cause).

pylint 4.0.7, astroid 4.0.4, Python 3.14.3; also on main 03eaf44a.

issue_snapshot.title: Reject conflicting duplicate Content-Length headers
issue_snapshot.body:
h2 currently accepts request header blocks that contain multiple content-length fields with conflicting values. In src/h2/stream.py (line 1367), _initialize_content_length() uses the first content-length it sees and returns immediately, so later conflicting values remain in the emitted headers but are not considered for body length validation.

This can create parser disagreement for applications, proxies, or protocol translators layered on top of h2: h2 may accept a message based on the first value while downstream code may use the last value, combine values, or reject the request. That shape is request-smuggling-prone.

issue_snapshot.title: S3 PutObject crashes when using non-seekable stream
issue_snapshot.body:
### Describe the bug

Passing a non-seekable stream to `put_object` fails with a signature error:

```
$ uv run --with boto3 python -c '
import io
import boto3

class NonSeekableStream(io.RawIOBase):
    def __init__(self, data):
        self._data = data
        self._pos = 0

    def read(self, n=-1):
        if n == -1:
            n = len(self._data) - self._pos
        chunk = self._data[self._pos : self._pos + n]
        self._pos += len(chunk)
        return chunk

    def readable(self):
        return True

s3 = boto3.client("s3")
s3.put_object(
    Bucket="mybucket-test-sync",
    Key="test.txt",
    Body=NonSeekableStream(b"hello world"),
    ContentLength=11,
)

'
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 21, in <module>
  File ".cache/uv/archive-v0/yqGESA53aCEP9s53_l_I4/lib/python3.12/site-packages/botocore/client.py", line 602, in _api_call
    return self._make_api_call(operation_name, kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".cache/uv/archive-v0/yqGESA53aCEP9s53_l_I4/lib/python3.12/site-packages/botocore/context.py", line 123, in wrapper
    return func(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".cache/uv/archive-v0/yqGESA53aCEP9s53_l_I4/lib/python3.12/site-packages/botocore/client.py", line 1078, in _make_api_call
    raise error_class(parsed_response, operation_name)
botocore.exceptions.ClientError: An error occurred (SignatureDoesNotMatch) when calling the PutObject operation: The request signature we calculated does not match the signature you provided. Check your key and signing method.
```

Compared to a seekable stream which works without issue:

```
$ uv run --with boto3 python -c '
import io
import boto3

s3 = boto3.client("s3")
s3.put_object(
    Bucket="mybucket-test-sync",
    Key="test.txt",
    Body=io.BytesIO(b"hello world"),
    ContentLength=11,
)

'
```

We can see that the SDK is sending an incompatible set of headers in its DEBUG output:

```
Content-Length: 11
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Content-Encoding: aws-chunked
```

This is explicitly disallowed in the HTTP RFC (7230), section 3.3:

>   that contains a Transfer-Encoding header field.

**StringToSign we calculate**

PUT

content-length:11
host:mybucket-test-sync.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
x-amz-content-sha256:STREAMING-UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD-TRAILER
x-amz-date:20260317T210735Z
x-amz-sdk-checksum-algorithm:CRC32
x-amz-trailer:x-amz-checksum-crc32

content-encoding;content-length;host;x-amz-content-sha256;x-amz-date;x-amz-sdk-checksum-algorithm;x-amz-trailer
STREAMING-UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD-TRAILER
```

**StringToSign from S3 error response**

Note the empty `content-length` with no value:

```
PUT
/test.txt

content-encoding:aws-chunked
content-length:
host:mybucket-test-sync.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
x-amz-content-sha256:STREAMING-UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD-TRAILER
x-amz-date:20260317T210735Z
x-amz-sdk-checksum-algorithm:CRC32

STREAMING-UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD-TRAILER

The input dtype to `scipy.linalg.signm` seems to only be preserved in certain cases and otherwise upcasts to `float64` (or `complex128`):

In [2]: signm(np.array([[2,1], [0,3]], np.float32))

issue_snapshot.title: Better heuristic for when to optimize `target()` metrics
issue_snapshot.body:
Currently, we run all of our optimizer routines [exactly once, starting at (or just after) half of our `max_examples` budget](https://github.com/HypothesisWorks/hypothesis/blob/9fce400120bcb7fcdf66626a5c6525f84db21e59/hypothesis-python/src/hypothesis/internal/conjecture/engine.py#L738-L743).  This works pretty well for the default `max_examples=100`, but I've noticed increasing use of Hypothesis with very large example budgets (and `target()`) for one-off searches for some example - and we can do much better for this workflow.  Specifically, we should:

- better support interleaving of ordinary generation with targeted optimization; e.g. "run an optimize step, then generate that many examples, then the next optimize step...".  This still aims to spend up-to-half our total examples optimizing.
- pick a smoother heuristic for when-to-optimize.  Initial proposal: maintain current behaviour for `max_examples < 1000`; for `max_examples >= 1000` use the incremental mixture instead, starting after 200 examples generated by our usual means.
- for long runs, we might finish running the optimizer.  How should we decide to start a second full pass?  We don't want unproductive re-runs (as may be implicated in #2985), but an additional run must *sometimes* make sense...

issue_snapshot.body:
The asyncio policy system is deprecated. The *event_loop_policy* fixture should be deprecated in favor of the *pytest_asyncio_loop_factories* hook. The deprecation is needed to inform users to migrate away from the fixture.

The goal of this task is that every user who reimplements *event_loop_policy* receives a *DeprecationWarning*. The warning message should state that the *event_loop_policy* fixture is deprecated and will be removed. It should also explain what functionality users should use instead (i.e. the *pytest_asyncio_loop_factories* hook).

## Possible implementation
A similar mechanism was needed for the deprecation of the *event_loop* fixture. This has previously been implemented by [setting an attribute](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-asyncio/blob/b24de088dbb92de2cedc506bcc4adb522a72bf7c/pytest_asyncio/plugin.py#L1127-L1132) on the original fixture definition provided by pytest-asyncio. Consequently, every fixture definition that didn't set the attribute caused a warning to be emitted.

issue_snapshot.title: httputil: Clean up HTTPServerRequest uri and start_line
issue_snapshot.body:
HTTPServerRequest has two redundant arguments, `uri` and `start_line`. If `start_line` is given, it takes precedence. All production code paths specify `start_line`, but some of tornado's test cases use `uri` only, and some third party test cases (`jupyter_server`) specify neither. 

Prior to https://github.com/tornadoweb/tornado/pull/3542, both were kind of optional (depending on what you did with the request object); since that PR it has been mandatory to specify one of them. This will make the upgrade to Tornado 6.6 mildly disruptive to at least `jupyter_server`.

* Consider replacing the assertions added in #3542 with deprecation warnings (and giving method/uri/version hard-coded defaults instead of None, to avoid supressing type warnings?). If not, give `jupyter_server` a heads up about `start_line` becoming mandatory.
* In 6.6: Add deprecation warnings when `method`, `uri`, or `version` are given non-None values, or when `start_line` is None
* In 6.7: Remove `method`, `uri`, `version` arguments, make other constructor arguments keyword-only, and make start_line mandatory
